common_core_categories.label: Curriculum coherence
common_core_categories.common_core_claim: A shared textbook can expose coherent sequencing, chapter goals, prerequisite progression, and links from concepts to exercises.
common_core_categories.overlay_need: Jurisdiction overlays must map local subject names, programme goals, standards codes, and mandatory sequence expectations.
common_core_categories.school_owned_boundary: Schools still own enacted curriculum, timetable choices, local schemes of work, and inspection conversations.

common_core_categories.label: Subject knowledge and progression
common_core_categories.common_core_claim: Scarcity, choice, opportunity cost, markets, demand/supply reasoning, data interpretation, and economic argumentation recur across the reviewed sources.
common_core_categories.overlay_need: Local overlays must add jurisdiction-specific vocabulary, examination taxonomies, and prescribed examples.
common_core_categories.school_owned_boundary: Textbook evidence does not prove student mastery or teacher diagnosis.

common_core_categories.label: Didactic quality
common_core_categories.common_core_claim: Worked examples, guided practice, independent practice, retrieval, feedback prompts, and misconception handling are portable product-design patterns.
common_core_categories.overlay_need: Inspectorate language and classroom evidence expectations vary strongly by jurisdiction.
common_core_categories.school_owned_boundary: Observed teaching quality, lesson adaptation, and classroom climate are school-owned.

common_core_categories.label: Assessment alignment
common_core_categories.common_core_claim: A shared bank can support formative checks, calculation/graph/source tasks, and argument construction.
common_core_categories.overlay_need: Exam-code mapping, mark schemes, assessment objectives, task forms, grading language, and national/state exam structures are local.
common_core_categories.school_owned_boundary: Summative validity, PTA/school assessment policy, and exam-board approval cannot be supplied by the textbook alone.

common_core_categories.label: Student support and differentiation
common_core_categories.common_core_claim: Scaffolding, hints, alternative representations, and difficulty layering can be designed into the shared product.
common_core_categories.overlay_need: Local SEN/SEND/inclusion/accommodation language and required documentation differ.
common_core_categories.school_owned_boundary: Individual support plans, intervention records, accommodations, and learner monitoring remain school-owned.

common_core_categories.label: Accessibility and inclusion
common_core_categories.common_core_claim: Semantic structure, readable layouts, text alternatives, keyboard support, contrast, and inclusive examples can be common product requirements.
common_core_categories.overlay_need: Legal standards, terminology, and proof expectations differ by country/state.
common_core_categories.school_owned_boundary: Accessibility certification, legal compliance, and individual accommodation evidence remain outside this foundation.

common_core_categories.label: Quality assurance
common_core_categories.common_core_claim: Source traceability, review records, validator checks, correction logs, and versioned evidence are portable product-quality controls.
common_core_categories.overlay_need: Each jurisdiction needs source freshness and authority-strength metadata.
common_core_categories.school_owned_boundary: School self-evaluation, governance, and official external review remain local/school-owned.

common_core_categories.label: Improvement cycle
common_core_categories.common_core_claim: Finding classification, owner next action, proof required to close, and review-after-correction are portable.
common_core_categories.overlay_need: Local accountability cycles and inspection timelines vary.
common_core_categories.school_owned_boundary: School improvement planning and accountable implementation are not textbook outputs.

common_core_categories.label: Safeguarding/product-school boundaries
common_core_categories.common_core_claim: The shared product can keep forbidden claims visible and avoid converting product evidence into school evidence.
common_core_categories.overlay_need: Safeguarding, privacy, and accountability vocabulary must be jurisdiction-specific.
common_core_categories.school_owned_boundary: Safeguarding practice, student data, school policy, and competent-authority judgement remain outside the textbook.

differences_matrix.finding: The Netherlands, Flanders, England, Italy, Poland, and parts of Spain use official inspection/supervision or national quality frameworks; the United States relies on federal/state accountability plus state/local standards and optional accreditation, not a national inspection regime.
differences_matrix.architecture_response: Keep school accountability evidence outside the shared textbook and route it to Layer 4.

differences_matrix.finding: Flanders is subnational, Germany and the United States require federal/context plus state/Land examples, and Spain requires autonomous-community overlays beyond national minimums.
differences_matrix.architecture_response: Require exact jurisdiction overlay descriptors and forbid generalized country claims where governance is subnational.

differences_matrix.finding: Some systems specify detailed programmes or examination content; others combine broad standards, competences, local curriculum design, and school-owned implementation.
differences_matrix.architecture_response: Layer 1 stores portable pedagogy; Layer 2 stores local curriculum mapping.

differences_matrix.finding: The Netherlands, France, Poland, and England use nationally regulated qualification or central-exam structures; US state examples and local districts vary; school assessment remains local in all cases.
differences_matrix.architecture_response: Layer 3 stores exam/assessment overlays and never claims summative validity from textbook tasks alone.

differences_matrix.finding: Quality frameworks ask for enacted curriculum, teaching, support, safety, results, improvement, and leadership evidence that a textbook can support but not supply.
differences_matrix.architecture_response: Layer 4 is school-owned and remains blocked for product claims.

differences_matrix.finding: Economic literacy often connects to civic, financial, enterprise, and data-literacy aims, but labels and obligations differ.
differences_matrix.architecture_response: Common core may include financial/economic reasoning; local overlays map citizenship/basic-skills labels.

differences_matrix.finding: Accessibility and inclusion are widely shared goals, but legal language, proof, and accommodations are local.
differences_matrix.architecture_response: Common product accessibility standards are allowed; compliance claims remain blocked.

differences_matrix.finding: Every reviewed governance system values evidence, but the form ranges from inspection evidence to exam specifications, school self-evaluation, and state standards documentation.
differences_matrix.architecture_response: All reports must preserve authority strength, allowed use, forbidden inference, and proof required to close.

finding_classification.finding: International common core is product-pedagogical, not jurisdiction-compliance.
finding_classification.does_not_block: Proceeding with common core and overlays as an internal analytical architecture.
finding_classification.proof_required_to_close: Keep overlays explicit and all blocked authority flags false.

finding_classification.blocks: All-Belgium, whole-UK, single-Germany, or national-US claims.
finding_classification.proof_required_to_close: Separate jurisdiction-specific source refresh before any local edition work.
